body.x: Massage devices have moved from specialist shops to everyday consumer electronics, and brands that sell them need new designs and functions every year to keep up with changing demand.
Guangdong Xinwei Health Technology says it answers that with a steady cycle of new models.

Guangdong Xinwei Health Technology Co., Ltd., a Dongguan-based maker of health and beauty products, is exhibiting six massage devices at KES 2026 and aims to show its R&D capabilities to global buyers. Luo Wei, the company's sales manager, represents it in the application.

The lineup includes the X201 calf massager, which has a 3 L airbag and a 4,000 mAh battery with dual temperature-control protection, and the X305 full-leg massager, which offers four timer modes, three massage types and five air pressure levels across six areas. The X805 head and scalp massager uses hand-simulating massage and vibration with red light therapy, and the X601 is a neck massager designed for use in cars. The X801 head massager adds Bluetooth music playback and 360-degree air pressure with heat, while the B401 foot massager combines multiple airbags with heating, red light therapy, EMS microcurrent and temperature control.

The company began operating in Hong Kong in 2011, opened its BEISIDE massage device factory in mainland China in 2017 and set up Guangdong Xinwei Health Technology in 2025. It has 10 to 15 R&D engineers and 5 to 10 sales staff. It says its products carry CE, RoHS, KC, FCC and UL certifications, and that its facility is certified under ISO 9001, ISO 13485 and the Business Social Compliance Initiative (BSCI). The company lists Samsung C&T, ALDI, TCHIBO, Ergobody, Mirum, Actto and Haan among its partners.

Its products are exported to South Korea, Japan, Turkey, the United States, Argentina and Germany, with South Korea and the United States showing the highest demand. The company is looking for brands that need customized or private-label massage device designs and for businesses seeking new functions and styles. It plans to raise production capacity and sales volume to two to three times current levels by 2027, expand its technical team in 2026 and start the FDA certification process. It names varying import requirements and certification standards across countries as a main challenge.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
